items.title: DeepSeek undercuts web search pricing
items.oneliner: DeepSeek priced live search and fetch at $0.75 per 1,000 requests, pushing retrieval costs toward commodity territory.

items.title: Lean now ships verified kernels
items.oneliner: Lean 4.35.0 ships verified kernels, bringing formal guarantees closer to production tooling instead of research demos.

items.title: Tao warns of a math split
items.oneliner: Terry Tao says LLMs could trigger a scientific golden age or a black-box dark age, depending on human oversight.

items.title: Researchers disclosed a KVM guest escape
items.oneliner: PwnEscape shows a guest-to-host KVM escape in Linux networking, a reminder that sandboxing still inherits kernel risk.

items.title: Targeted ads delivered mercenary spyware
items.oneliner: Citizen Lab linked targeted ads to zero-click Candiru spyware on 45 Al Jazeera devices, making adtech a security boundary.

items.title: Trusted execution still has trust gaps
items.oneliner: A fresh TEE critique argues attestation bugs and physical attacks keep SGX and SEV far shakier than vendors imply.

items.title: The NIST curve seed mystery ended
items.oneliner: Researchers traced NIST elliptic curve seeds to drand48 plus Unix timestamps, removing one long-running cryptography suspicion.

items.title: Websites are blocking AI agents
items.oneliner: Sites are increasingly blocking AI agents, which means agentic products now need fallback plans for a hostile web.

items.title: Go shipped interactive refactoring support
items.oneliner: gopls added interactive refactoring and proposed an LSP pattern other languages can copy for safer large-scale edits.

items.title: GNOME is turning its OS serious
items.oneliner: GNOME OS Preview graduates from nightly experiment to stable preview, signaling a real push toward an end-user Linux platform.
